title: Conjecture 11
statement_text: If $G$ is a universally cell 3-colorable graph which does not have a subcontraction isomorphic to $K^+_{3,n-3}$ for some $n \geq 7$, then $G$ is 3-flowable.
context_text: Graphs are finite multigraphs. A drawing of $G$ maps vertices to distinct points of the plane and edges to curves between their endpoints, with finitely many intersection points (edges may cross each other or themselves arbitrarily, and need not be simple drawings); its cells are the maximal connected regions of the plane minus the drawing. A cell $k$-coloring colors the cells with $k$ colors so that two cells sharing a segment of an edge get different colors. $G$ is universally cell $3$-colorable if every drawing of $G$ in the plane has a cell $3$-coloring. $G$ is $k$-flowable if it has a nowhere-zero $k$-flow, i.e. an orientation with arc weights in $\mathbb{Z}_k\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying flow conservation at every vertex. For $X\subseteq V(G)$, $G/X$ is obtained by replacing $X$ by a single new vertex $v_X$ joined by one edge to $u$ for each edge $uv$ with $u\notin X$, $v\in X$ (edges inside $X$ disappear; $X$ need not be connected); a subcontraction of $G$ is any graph obtained by a finite sequence of such identifications. $K^+_{3,n-3}$ is the $n$-vertex graph obtained from $K_{3,n-3}$ by adding an edge between two vertices of the part of size $3$. For planar graphs, universal cell $3$-colorability is equivalent to $3$-flowability; in general every $3$-flowable graph and every $4$-edge-connected graph is universally cell $3$-colorable, and the equivalence also holds for graphs of maximum degree at most $3$ and for $K_{3,3}$-minor-free graphs. The authors show that $K^+_{3,n-3}$ is universally cell $3$-colorable but not $3$-flowable for every $n\ge7$, and that universal cell $3$-colorability is closed under subcontractions. Having found no other examples beyond simple modifications of these, they conjecture that excluding them as subcontractions restores the equivalence. A positive answer would imply Tutte's 3-flow conjecture (every $4$-edge-connected graph is $3$-flowable), since $4$-edge-connectivity is preserved by subcontractions and $K^+_{3,n-3}$ has a vertex of degree $3$.

title: Tutte's 3-Flow Conjecture
context_text: Tutte's 3-Flow Conjecture is a long-standing central open problem in the theory of nowhere-zero flows. The paper formulates Conjecture 11 about universal cell 3-colorability and proves (Claim 13) that Conjecture 11 implies Tutte's 3-Flow Conjecture. The paper also proves Conjecture 11 for subcubic graphs and for $K_{3,3}$-minor-free graphs, yielding partial progress toward Tutte's conjecture in those graph classes.
paper_contribution: Shows that the authors' Conjecture 11 (on universal cell 3-colorability without $K^+_{3,n-3}$ subcontractions) implies Tutte's 3-Flow Conjecture; establishes Conjecture 11 for subcubic and $K_{3,3}$-minor-free graphs, giving new special-case confirmations of Tutte's conjecture.
notes: Cited as Conjecture 1.1.8 in Zhang [24]. The paper's Corollary 7 independently reproves that every 4-edge-connected graph is universally cell 3-colorable, consistent with but not resolving Tutte's conjecture.
